blocks.raw: # Starting Collections
blocks.text: Starting Collections

blocks.raw: ## Collection Schedule
blocks.text: Collection Schedule

blocks.raw: The Collection Schedule is used to hold the information on the payment’s frequency, the payment amount, and currency. For example, a Collection Schedule can be set up to collect £100 on 15th of every month for the next 12 months. Modulr will then automatically create individual Collections to receive payments as per the schedule. Collection Schedules can also be set up to collect a one-off payment.
blocks.text: The Collection Schedule is used to hold the information on the payment’s frequency, the payment amount, and currency. For example, a Collection Schedule can be set up to collect £100 on 15th of every month for the next 12 months. Modulr will then automatically create individual Collections to receive payments as per the schedule. Collection Schedules can also be set up to collect a one-off payment.

blocks.raw: Collection Schedules can be set up to collect a certain amount as a first payment and a different amount as the regular recurring payment. For example, you can specify that the first payment is for £200 on 20th April, and the regular recurring payments should be on a monthly basis for of £100 to be collected on the 1st of every month. The regular recurring amount needs to be for the same amount. If the collection amount will vary then a new Collection Schedule needs to be made for each collection. Please note that every time a new single collection is requested the Payer needs to be notified of this new amount; this is something you will need to make sure happens as it is a rule of the Direct Debit scheme.

blocks.raw: **Advance Notice**
blocks.text: Advance Notice

blocks.raw: At least 3 working days’ Advance notice must be given by our Partner to their customers before the first Direct Debit is collected in the form of an email.
blocks.text: At least 3 working days’ Advance notice must be given by our Partner to their customers before the first Direct Debit is collected in the form of an email.

blocks.raw: Advance notice must be given before the first collection but is not required for subsequent collections. Advance notice must also be given if the Service User makes any changes to the Direct Debit amount, due date or frequency. The timescale of this communication, or advance notice period, must adhere to what was originally advised in the Direct Debit Guarantee, and must also be delivered by the method of communication as advised to the Payer. For re-presentable collections, no advance notice is needed again.

blocks.raw: ## Core Referencing
blocks.text: Core Referencing

blocks.raw: When creating the collection schedule, an additional optional parameter `collectionReference` can be included which will be suffixed to the mandate reference on collection requests. This change makes it easier for payers to identify corresponding debits on their account when using a mandate (DDI) for multiple purposes.
blocks.text: When creating the collection schedule, an additional optional parameter collectionReference can be included which will be suffixed to the mandate reference on collection requests. This change makes it easier for payers to identify corresponding debits on their account when using a mandate (DDI) for multiple purposes.

blocks.raw: Each collection can now have a core reference inherited from the Mandate (DDI) and separate suffix, allowing the collection of multiple Direct Debit agreements under the same mandate and on the same day.
blocks.text: Each collection can now have a core reference inherited from the Mandate (DDI) and separate suffix, allowing the collection of multiple Direct Debit agreements under the same mandate and on the same day.

blocks.raw: The `collectionReference` and core mandate reference combined can be up to a maximum of 18 characters.
blocks.text: The collectionReference and core mandate reference combined can be up to a maximum of 18 characters.

blocks.raw: **Happy Path**
blocks.text: Happy Path

blocks.raw: Day 1:
blocks.text: Day 1:

blocks.raw:
1. The Collection Schedule triggers Collection request to start the process of collecting funds from the Partner’s customer.
2. Modulr generates a file that includes collection amount from the customer.
3. Modulr’s cut-off time is at 3:30PM, as Modulr needs to transform the file into a format accepted by BACS. The status changes to “**Processing**”.
4. At 5:10PM, Modulr sends the file to the Scheme
5. Collection Schedule creates a collection request for the next due date.

blocks.raw: ## Collection Statuses
blocks.text: Collection Statuses

blocks.raw:
* **Scheduled** - Collection Request is created and waiting to be sent to BACS.
* **Processing** - Collection Request has been sent to BACS.
* **Success** - Collection has not received an ARUDDs and on Day 5, we consider them a successful collection.
* **Cancelled** - Partner cancels the collection request.
* **Failed** - Partner cancels the collections request or collection is failed because the reason was not representable.
* **Representable** - Upon receiving an ARUDDs, BACS tells Modulr if the collection can be retried.
* **Represented** - Partner retries on a representable collection.

blocks.raw: ## Representment of unpaid Direct Debits
blocks.text: Representment of unpaid Direct Debits

blocks.raw: A Direct Debit that has been returned unpaid with a status of **Representable** may be retried using the [represent collection ](https://modulr.readme.io/reference/representcollection)endpoint. There are specific scheme rules about the ability to represent and process in the Service Users Guide and Rules to the Direct Debit Scheme that must be followed - see extract below:

There are specific scheme rules about the ability to represent and process in the Service Users Guide and Rules to the Direct Debit Scheme that must be followed - see extract below:

blocks.raw: *Re-presentation of an unpaid Direct Debit may continue for****one month**** from the date on which first presentation was made.*

Refer to section 4B ‘Advance notice’.f the Service Users Guide and Rules to the Direct Debit Scheme]\_

* *If the Direct Debit has been returned for the reason ‘refer to payer’ then additional advance notice is not mandatory but is recommended.*

blocks.raw: ## Sandbox
blocks.text: Sandbox

blocks.raw:
**Creating your first mandate on the Sandbox**
Once set up, the first logical step is to try to use the POST /accounts/\{id}/mandates endpoint to [create a mandate](https://modulr.readme.io/reference/createmandate). Typically, when you have built your user interface, your app will be using this endpoint to send through the information to Modulr that was entered by your customers in your mandate form.
blocks.text:

Typically, when you have built your user interface, your app will be using this endpoint to send through the information to Modulr that was entered by your customers in your mandate form.

* Only upper case characters are allowed, so any alphabetic characters supplied in this string will be converted to upper case before processing.

blocks.raw:
**Mocking collection activity**
Since there are no actual collections on Sandbox, there needs to be some way to test the integration. In order to achieve this we have a Sandbox-only endpoint, POST /external-services-mock/collections, that allows you to add the required collections and then call GET /collections to retrieve the expected collection activity.
blocks.text:
Mocking collection activity
Since there are no actual collections on Sandbox, there needs to be some way to test the integration. In order to achieve this we have a Sandbox-only endpoint, POST /external-services-mock/collections, that allows you to add the required collections and then call GET /collections to retrieve the expected collection activity.

```json
[   
    {
      "activityDate": "2020-06-25",
      "amount": 50.00,
      "collectionScheduleBid": "Q120026P",
      "customerReference" :  "DDI12347",
      "originalActivityDate": "2020-06-25",

      "status" : "H",
```

**Things to note:**
The dates in the call should be tomorrow's date, or date for which you will attempt to GET collections. We process mocked collections on daily schedule. I.e. if you create a mock call today, you will be able to retrieve the collections through the GET call tomorrow.

<Callout icon="📘" theme="info">
  ### How are returned direct debits treated?

  If there is a collection failure due to any reason (such as insufficient funds), you will know the next working day via [Webhook - Direct Debit, DD Collection Status](https://modulr.readme.io/docs/webhook-direct-debit-ddcollectionstatus) after the funds has been credited to your account.

  On rare occasions, you might be made aware of a rejected one more day later. This is referred to as a "late cancellation" and is deemed an exceptional scenario, but one that the BACS scheme allows to happen. The funds of that return will be deducted from the settlement account.
</Callout>

blocks.raw:
<Callout icon="📘" theme="info">
  ### What is the indemnity claim challenge  process?

  If you are a Service User with contacts on the Bacs Payment Services website (PSW) you will be notified of Direct Debit Indemnity Claims (DDIC) via this channel & can manage challenges here.

  If Modulr is the service user on you behalf, you should contact Modulr customer services (after having found out about the indemnity via email) to challenge the claim. Modulr will then pass on to the Direct Debit scheme.

  A Direct Debit Indemnity claim can be challenged in certain circumstances by providing evidence to refute the claim, this must be done within 10 days of the claim being received. If successful the claim will be cancelled by the paying PSP; their decision is final on any DDIC challenge.
</Callout>

blocks.raw:
<Callout icon="📘" theme="info">
  ### Is the Direct Debit collection account only able to be used for Direct Debit collections?

  Technically the account is a Faster Payments account that has the Direct Debit collection product added to it, and the collection payments are actually Faster Payments. Also payments out would be Faster Payments and can be made as needed. Payments in should be restricted to DD collections as otherwise other payments will confuse any reconciliation. If you need another way to get funds, e.g. for customers to make non DD ad-hoc payments, then you should create other accounts for that purpose (ideally one per one of your customers).
</Callout>

  ### Are custom schedules (different amounts per collection) available?

  Yes, but not in the same collection schedule; to collect a different amount you will need to set up a new scheduled collection (with "ONCE" frequency) for each different amount under the same mandate.

blocks.raw:
### How do you handle retries? If a collection fails for a reason that can be retried (e.g. Refer to payer), the transaction status will be updated to REPRESENTABLE and notified the [Webhook - Direct Debit, DD Collection Status](https://modulr.readme.io/docs/webhook-direct-debit-ddcollectionstatus).
A transaction with this status can be resubmitted using the /[represent ](https://modulr.readme.io/reference/representcollection)endpoint - the Direct Debit scheme rules must be followed. Practically as representation should only take place up to one month from the original collection date, this allows for a maximum of 3 representations (allowing for notice)
